hint: Quotient rule: $\left(\frac{u}{v}\right)' = \frac{u'v - uv'}{v^2}$. The order on top matters.

hints.text: Quotient rule: $\left(\frac{u}{v}\right)' = \frac{u'v - uv'}{v^2}$. The order on top matters.
The top simplifies to $-7$, so $g'(x) = \frac{-7}{(x - 3)^2}$ and $g'(4) = \frac{-7}{1} = -7$.

explanation: Top of the quotient rule: $u'v - uv' = 2(x - 3) - (2x + 1) = 2x - 6 - 2x - 1 = -7$.
At $x = 4$: $\frac{-7}{(1)^2} = -7$. The graph is falling steeply just right of its asymptote at $x = 3$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Rewrite, then differentiate
steps: The constant $2$ has derivative $0$, and $\frac{7}{x - 3} = 7(x - 3)^{-1}$ has derivative $-7(x - 3)^{-2}$.
At $x = 4$: $-7 \cdot 1 = -7$. Same answer, no quotient rule needed.
